title: Forwarding commutes with applying an action
statement: Let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $\iota:S\to H$, choose $r\in H$, and let $p$ be a Boolean word. For any action $a$ and configuration $c$ of a Boolean machine with $k$ work tapes and state set $S$, applying the action that preserves $a$'s tape operations and output and maps its successor state through $\iota$ (using $r$ if it halts) to the configuration that maps $c$'s state through $\iota$ (using $r$ if it is halted) and prefixes its output by $p$ yields the forwarded image of the result of applying $a$ to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A map $\iota:S\to H$ and designated state $r\in H$
An action $a$ and configuration $c$ with $k$ work tapes, Boolean alphabet, and state set $S
replaced:
Let $S$ and $H$ be sets of states, $\iota : S \to H$, $r \in H$, and $p$ a Boolean word.
For every action $a$ and every configuration $c$ of a Boolean Turing machine with $k$
work tapes and state set $S$ on an input $x$, applying the forwarding transform of $a$
(same head moves, writes and emission as $a$, successor mapped through $\iota$, a halt
replaced by $r$) to the forwarding image of $c$ (state mapped through $\iota$, or $r$ if
$c$ is halted, the same tapes and heads, output $p$ followed by the output of $c$) gives
the forwarding image of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$.
